ignore.reason: Logged at err during boot on both VMs: something at boot looks for the virtual CD-ROM, but the VM has no sr0 device (not in /sys/block). Not a hardware fault.

notes.cpu: B2ats_v2 is burstable: base CPU is 20% (60 initial credits, 24 banked per hour, max 576). These numbers are measured while bursting; with no credits left the CPU drops to about a fifth, which looks like a fault but is the platform throttling.
notes.disk: The OS disk has host caching ReadWrite (checked with the instance metadata service). The 256 MB fio file is served from the host's cache, so IOPS (~9,400) is far above the P6 disk's own limit (3,500 when bursting). Good for spotting drift, not a measure of the disk itself.
notes.network: Azure caps this size at 6,250 Mbps in total; one TCP stream measured 4.8-5.0 Gbit/s between the two nodes.

notes.cpu.logical_cpus: Azure vCPU = logical CPU (on this size: 1 core x 2 hyperthreads).
notes.memory.min_ratio: MemTotal is RAM minus firmware/kernel reservations. Measured 0.82 GiB of 1 GiB; small VMs lose a bigger share. Use ~0.95 for large servers.
notes.disk.check_type: Azure virtual disks report rotational=1 even on Premium SSD, so disk type can't be verified here. Set true on bare metal.
notes.nics: Only presence and link state. The driver claims 50 Gbit/s but 4.84 was measured; speed is checked by benchmarks.
notes.kernel_log.max_priority: Count messages at priority 0-3 (emerg, alert, crit, err). Warnings (4) are only counted: a healthy VM logs 9 at boot (no PCI bus, no CPU microcode, ...).
notes.kernel_log.ignore: Known harmless messages (regex, matched with re.search). Each needs a reason, so every exception is on record.
notes.benchmark.runs: Each benchmark runs 3 times and the median is kept, so one slow run (a noisy neighbour) doesn't move the baseline.
notes.benchmark.compare: Per metric: which way is better, and how much worse than the baseline gives WARN or FAIL. warn_drop / fail_drop are shares of the baseline: bandwidth varied 7% within one baseline and 14% between two sessions (5.03 vs 5.73 Gbit/s), so 15% / 25% leave room for that. warn_by / fail_by are in the metric's unit: latency is about 0.46 ms, and with no fault it was up to 0.64 ms higher on the same evening (+139%), so a percentage would flag noise; 2 ms of added delay showed as +2.36 ms. Better than the baseline is never flagged. A metric without thresholds is shown but not judged.
